questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A country outside of Europe, nature close by, not necessarily a huge city

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - they send lots of emails up until the arrival

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had sent out detailed e-mails in terms of where to pick up the keys for the apartments, introduction to the different courses, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You could choose between Nipisiy house (4- or 6-bedroom apartments), International House (own room and bathroom, but shared kitchen with the floor), and HUB (2- or 4-bedroom apartments)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are canteens in Lister and Peter Loughead residences, offering meal-plans, but I didn't buy them, so I don't know much about it. The kitchens are generally good, but they come un-equipped, so you have to buy your own pots, pans, knives, forks, plates, etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would recommend staying in Nipisiy. I stayed in a 6-bedroom apartment and it was great. There are three bathrooms, a huge kitchen with two stoves, two fridges, lots of space in general and it is a two-story apartment. From what I've heard, it can get quite lonely living in International House if you don't talk to anyone on your floor. When living with 5 other people you have the option to hang out in the kitchen/living room/common area together, or you can go to your room if you want to be alone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only thing about on-campus housing is that it is quite expensive, but it is worth it, because you get to meet people you otherwise wouldn't have met

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They sent out a VERY long pdf step by-step. And even though it was a step-by-step guide, it was still a bit difficult to follow and some of the things we had to fill out just did not make sense. The process is long and in my opinion they could make it a lot less complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mailing the person in charge of exchange students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The classes filled up fairly quickly, but there is a watchlist (waitlist) available, and a lot of people drop out of classes last minute / close to the semester start. So I managed to get all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the instructions carefully

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses varied in levels. Some were a lot more difficult than expected (aka same level as Copenhagen University), some were easier to follow. There were lots of assignments throughout the semester that counted towards your final grade, which meant that there was quite a lot of work to get done throughout the semester. This is just something to be aware of when choosing courses. You could also choose courses that count 100% towards your final grade instead of 40% midterm assignment and then 60% final exam for example.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At home, the professors are better at engaging the students whereas at U of A, the professors talk for 1,5 hours, which can be very tiring. They are not as good with breaks, which I could definitely feel that I was used to from home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Corporations, Judgment Enforcement Law, Canadian Human Rights Law, Intellectual Property, Professionalism and Ethics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Canadian Human Rights Law was my favourite - the professor is good and the course is very interesting and relevant.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to buy everything. You have to buy your own duvet, pillow, hangers, kitchen things, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are quite expensive, but similar to prices in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not attend any clubs

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can watch the school hockey games for free, and there is a huge gym that is free as well, which was very nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Watch hockey games

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains or cities like Vancouver, Toronto, Montreal

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them from the very beginning of classes - Canadians are extremely friendly and are interested in learning about you and your culture

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The level of friendliness can sometimes be a little too much

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: On the other hand, I very much appreciated the kindness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The campus area and Whyte Avenue are the nice areas. 
Spend your weekends away from Edmonton - experience Banff, Jasper, the Rockies.
Choose courses that does not require you to spend your weekends writing assignments.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are some good deals through the university - fx renting cars from Enterprise!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people that I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning - meeting everyone, figuring out where you fit in and also adjusting to the Canadian law system and the way they teach

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
